skill.name: read-github
skill.description: Access GitHub repository documentation and code search through the gitmcp.io MCP service. Use it when an assistant needs repository context, documentation answers, or code references.
skill.summary: Fetch and search GitHub repository docs and code through GitMCP.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: The script intentionally runs `npx -y mcp-remote` and sends repository requests to gitmcp.io, so the meaningful risks are external command execution, third-party network routing, and weak URL validation. Most SKILL.md backtick findings are false positives from Markdown formatting, and I found no prompt-injection text in the reviewed files. Publication should require changes around package pinning, URL allowlisting, and clearer data-sharing disclosures.

remediation.suggestion: Pin mcp-remote to a reviewed version or vendor a wrapper. Require explicit confirmation before first npm package execution.
Reject non-GitHub URLs and require a strict owner/repo or github.com allowlist before calling mcp-remote.
Validate fetch-url targets, restrict schemes to https, and require user confirmation before fetching external URLs.
Document that repository names, search queries, and requested URLs are sent to gitmcp.io.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary MCP Server URL Accepted
semantic_findings.description: convert_github_to_gitmcp returns non-GitHub HTTP input unchanged, and main passes the result into mcp-remote. A malicious prompt could make the assistant connect to an untrusted MCP server instead of gitmcp.io.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code explicitly preserves arbitrary HTTP URLs and launches mcp-remote with the derived value. The intended interface says GitHub repos, so this bypass is a clear context-level risk.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted External URL Fetch Tool
semantic_findings.description: The fetch-url command accepts a user-provided URL and passes it to fetch_generic_url_content. This can retrieve arbitrary external content through the GitMCP service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command-line parser accepts any URL string and forwards it to the remote tool without local allowlisting. The impact is bounded by remote service policies, so confidence and severity are medium.

content.value_statement: Repository documentation can be slow to inspect from an AI chat. This skill uses GitMCP to fetch docs, search docs, and search code.
actual_capabilities: Converts GitHub URLs and owner/repo paths to GitMCP endpoints.
Lists available GitMCP tools for a repository.
Fetches repository documentation through the GitMCP MCP service.
Searches repository documentation with semantic queries.
Searches repository code for exact strings through GitHub search.
Fetches referenced URL content through GitMCP when requested.
limitations: Requires network access to gitmcp.io and npm tooling for mcp-remote.
Private repository access is not described by the skill.
Fetched URLs must be accepted by GitMCP and remote site policies.
Tool names depend on repository names and may fail for unusual names.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a New Library
use_cases.description: Review repository documentation before deciding whether a dependency fits a project.

use_cases.title: Answer Repository Questions
use_cases.description: Find setup steps, features, and usage guidance without browsing files manually.

use_cases.title: Trace API Usage
use_cases.description: Search documentation and code for functions, classes, or configuration names.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the documentation for owner/repo and summarize what the project does, who uses it, and the main setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Find Setup Instructions
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the docs for owner/repo and identify installation, configuration, and first-run guidance. Include any version requirements you find.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Docs and Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch the docs for owner/repo, then search code for the main API names. Explain whether the documentation matches the implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Feature Path
prompt_templates.prompt: Use documentation search and code search in owner/repo to trace how a named feature works. Report key files, concepts, and open questions.

output_examples.input: Read the docs for facebook/react and explain the main setup path.
output_examples.output: A concise project overview, setup summary, and pointers to the most relevant documentation sections.

output_examples.input: Search owner/repo for authentication configuration guidance.
output_examples.output: A short list of matching documentation topics, with plain-language notes about each relevant result.

output_examples.input: Find where a feature is documented and implemented in a repository.
output_examples.output: A combined documentation and code summary that names likely files and explains how the feature is connected.

best_practices: Start with fetch-docs before using narrower searches.
Use specific search terms from the repository documentation.
Confirm important answers against code search when accuracy matters.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for private repositories unless access and data handling are clear.
Do not fetch unrelated external URLs from repository content.
Do not treat search results as complete without checking the main documentation.

faq.question: What does this skill connect to?
faq.answer: It connects to the gitmcp.io MCP service through the mcp-remote command.

faq.question: Can it search code as well as docs?
faq.answer: Yes. The script includes documentation search and exact code search commands.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. It needs network access for gitmcp.io, npm package resolution, and remote repository data.

faq.question: Is it suitable for private repositories?
faq.answer: The skill does not describe private repository authentication or data controls.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users verify?
faq.answer: Users should verify that repository names, search queries, and fetched URLs are safe to send to GitMCP.
